key_insight: ImageNet pretraining improved vocal fold boundary segmentation in both transformer-based models, with roughly fourfold greater gains for Swin-UNet than TransUNet.
engineering_relevance: Automated segmentation could reduce manual processing in intraglottal PIV, supporting measurements of vocal fold motion and airflow under challenging optical conditions.
method: Benchmarked CNN-based UNet and UNet++, hybrid TransUNet, and transformer-based Swin-UNet.
Compared TransUNet and Swin-UNet trained from scratch versus ImageNet-pretrained weights.
Evaluated overlap and boundary fidelity using DSC, BF1, and HD95.
evidence_signal: Six pipelines were trained with five seeds using 16,344 expert-annotated images from 227 ex vivo canine phonation trials and evaluated on 50 held-out trials with Holm-corrected Wilcoxon tests; mean DSC ranged from 0.9734 to 0.9764.
watch_item: Generalization beyond ex vivo canine intraglottal PIV images remains unestablished.
paper_title: Effects of Deep Learning Architecture and Pretraining on Automated Vocal Fold Segmentation in Ex Vivo High-Speed Phonation Images
